title: MoGA: Mixture-of-Groups Attention for End-to-End Long Video Generation
claim: Dense and block-level sparse attention are costly or unreliable; routing tokens into learned groups gives efficient, accurate sparse attention.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, red failure labels versus green ours panel
description: Three side-by-side rounded panels share a column of input video tokens (pink squares) at the top, with a small three-frame input video strip at far left showing a boy and a green dog. (a) Full Attention is a light-blue panel showing Q, K and V arrows into a large grey attention-score matrix, with a softmax-weight arrow and a red sad face labelled 'Dense Compute'. (b) Block Sparse Attention shows pooled token blocks and a grid similarity map with green check marks and red crosses, a blue-to-green similarity-score colorbar, and the red label 'Similarity Confusion'. (c) Mixture-of-Groups Attention is a green panel stacking Token Router, Group Self-Attention (Group 1 to Group M) and Token Rearranger, ending with a green smiley and 'Efficient Sparse'. Red versus green coloring draws the eye to the contrast.
caption: Illustration of our motivation. (a) Full attention suffers from dense computing when dealing with long sequences. (b) Block sparse attention [ref] may fail when block-level similarity is confused, resulting in unreliable attention. (c) Mixture-of-Groups attention uses a lightweight token router (i.e., a single linear layer) that assigns tokens to specialized groups, enabling groupwise attention and efficient long-context modeling.
abstract: Long video generation with Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) is bottlenecked by the quadratic scaling of full attention with sequence length. Since attention is highly redundant, outputs are dominated by a small subset of query-key pairs. Existing sparse methods rely on blockwise coarse estimation, whose accuracy-efficiency trade-offs are constrained by block size. This paper introduces Mixture-of-Groups Attention (MoGA), an efficient sparse attention that uses a lightweight, learnable token router to precisely match tokens without blockwise estimation. Through semantic-aware routing, MoGA enables effective long-range interactions. As a kernel-free method, MoGA integrates seamlessly with modern attention stacks, including FlashAttention and sequence parallelism. Building on MoGA, we develop an efficient long video generation model that end-to-end produces minute-level, multi-shot, 480p videos at 24 fps, with a context length of approximately 580k. Comprehensive experiments on various video generation tasks validate the effectiveness of our approach.
